complexity.notes: Correct but unidiomatic: `valid *= isValidLine(...)` accumulates via integer multiplication and never short-circuits, so all 27 checks always run; `valid = valid and isValidLine(...)` (or `&=`) would be clearer and allow early exit. `line.count(num)` makes each line check quadratic in line length; a single pass with a ||set of seen values|| would be linear, though irrelevant at this fixed size. `List` is used without importing it from `typing`, which only works because LeetCode's environment pre-imports it. Amusingly, the deferred annotation rules of CPython 3.14 mean nothing here — these annotations are all fine anyway.
complexity.summary: Extracts each row, column (via list comprehension), and 3x3 box (via slicing), then validates each line by checking that no non-empty cell's count exceeds 1.
